title: History providers
summary: A history provider loads and stores the transcript for each run. The built-in one keeps messages in the session. You can swap in a database provider, add an audit provider and choose when persistence happens.
useIf: Conversation history must live in your own store, be audited, shrink under a reducer, or be written after every model call.
avoidIf: The provider already manages the conversation (Foundry agents, Responses with `store` on) and you do not need local copies.

explain.md: **Two storage modes.** *Local session state*: full history in `AgentSession.state`, usually via `InMemoryHistoryProvider` (default source id `in_memory`, may be auto-added by `RawAgent`). *Service-managed*: the service keeps the conversation and the session holds a `service_session_id`. Configured local history providers are skipped when a session is service-managed [[tr11]].

**Rules.** Configure only one history provider with `load_messages=True`. Add audit or evaluation providers with `load_messages=False` and `store_context_messages=True` so they also capture context other providers injected. A custom provider must not keep per-session data on the instance (one instance serves all sessions): keep database keys in session state. In .NET override `ProvideChatHistoryAsync` and `StoreChatHistoryAsync` of `ChatHistoryProvider` and use `ProviderSessionState<T>`; in Python implement `get_messages` and `save_messages` on `HistoryProvider` [[tr11]] [[tr12]].

**When it persists.** By default local providers persist once after the whole run. With `require_per_service_call_history_persistence=True` (Python) they run around every model call, which helps if middleware can end a run right after a tool call. It raises an error if the run is bound to a service-managed conversation. The Harness requires the per-call mode [[tr11]]. To bound size, .NET `InMemoryChatHistoryProvider` takes a `ChatReducer` such as `MessageCountingChatReducer(20)`; compaction is the richer option [[tr13]].

blocks.code:
class DatabaseHistoryProvider(HistoryProvider):
    def __init__(self, db):
        super().__init__('db-history', load_messages=True)
        self._db = db                       # a client, never a per-session key

    async def get_messages(self, session_id, *, state=None, **kw):
        key = (state or {}).get('history_key', session_id or 'default')
        return [Message.from_dict(r) for r in await self._db.load_messages(key)]

    async def save_messages(self, session_id, messages, *, state=None, **kw):
        if messages:
            key = state.setdefault('history_key', session_id or 'default') if state is not None else (session_id or 'default')
            await self._db.save_messages(key, [m.to_dict() for m in messages])

agent = Agent(client=client,
    context_providers=[DatabaseHistoryProvider(db),
                       InMemoryHistoryProvider('audit', load_messages=False,
                                               store_context_messages=True)],
    require_per_service_call_history_persistence=True)

whereToUse: Compliance: store full transcripts in your database with your retention rules
Multi-instance services where any node must load a conversation
Audit and evaluation capture beside the primary history
Long tool loops where each model call should be durable

use: You must own retention, deletion and encryption of conversation data
You need compaction or provider switching, which require local history
A crash mid-run must not lose completed model calls
avoid: The provider's managed conversation is enough and policy permits it
Per-call persistence on a service-managed run: it raises an error
Putting a session key in a provider field: it leaks across sessions
flips: Provider-side retention is acceptable and you want the least code: use service-managed history and drop compaction
Transcripts must carry injected context for audit: add a second provider with `store_context_messages=True`

pitfalls.symptom: Messages are duplicated or ordering is odd
pitfalls.fix: Keep exactly one loader; make others audit-only

pitfalls.cause: A provider stored the database key in an instance field
pitfalls.fix: Store per-session keys in session state (`ProviderSessionState` or the Python `state` dict)

pitfalls.symptom: Raises an error on start with per-call persistence
pitfalls.fix: Use it only with framework-managed local history

scenarios.title: Regulated transcripts with 7-year retention
scenarios.situation: A bank assistant must retain full transcripts for 7 years in its own database, deletable on request. Tool loops can run 20 model calls.
unknowns: Is the transcript allowed to include injected context?
scenarios.question: How do you store history?

options.name: Custom history provider backed by your database, per-call persistence on, an audit provider with context capture
options.why: You control retention and deletion, each model call is durable, and context injected by other providers is captured.
options.tradeoff: You build and test the provider and the schema.

options.name: Service-managed Responses conversations
options.why: Retention and deletion are the provider's, and compaction cannot apply.
options.tradeoff: Fine when provider retention satisfies policy.

options.name: In-memory history saved as a session blob at the end of each run
options.tradeoff: A crash mid-run loses the calls since the last save, and queries across conversations are hard.

flips.if: Privacy rules forbid storing tool results
flips.then: Filter in the provider before saving, and keep the audit provider off.
A session blob in your database may suffice.

scenarios.takeaway: Own the store when retention is a legal duty.

scenarios.title: Prototype demo for a hackathon
scenarios.situation: A two-day prototype with three users. No data policy applies. The team wants speed.
unknowns: Will it survive past the demo?
Does it need to switch models?
scenarios.question: What history setup?

options.name: Default in-memory history in the session
options.why: Zero setup, portable across models, easy to upgrade later.
options.tradeoff: Loses state on restart; add persistence if the demo lives on.

options.name: A custom database provider from day one
options.tradeoff: Right once real users and retention rules exist.

options.name: Service-managed conversation
options.tradeoff: Locks history to the provider and disables compaction.

flips.then: Replace the provider and add session persistence before onboarding real data.

scenarios.takeaway: Start in memory; move the store when state must outlive the process.

options: Two history providers load messages; only one should use `load_messages=True`
The audit provider needs a database
quiz.explain: Only one history provider should load messages. Audit providers use `load_messages=False` and `store_context_messages=True`.

quiz.q: You enabled a compaction pipeline on an agent that uses Foundry service-managed history, yet token usage did not fall. Why?
options: Compaction applies only to agents that hold history in memory, and has no effect on service-managed history
quiz.explain: The docs state compaction has no effect on Foundry agents, Responses with `store` on or Copilot Studio.

flashcards.front: How should audit history providers be configured?
flashcards.back: `load_messages=False` and `store_context_messages=True`, so they capture injected context without loading it back.

flashcards.front: What does per-service-call history persistence change?
flashcards.back: History providers run around every model call instead of once per run. It errors on service-managed runs, and the Harness requires it.

flashcards.front: Where must a custom provider keep a session's database key?
flashcards.back: In session state, never on the provider instance, because one instance serves all sessions.
